Subject: Re: Security exhibit / audit rights clarification for order form

Chris — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the specifics; made progress on a proposal and attached a draft Security Exhibit for the order form (sec_exhibit_draft_v1.pdf) and an evidence manifest template. Highlights:

- SOC 2: Redwood will provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report within 7 business days of counter-signature; we will include a redacted report and a signed letter confirming there are no open exceptions impacting customer data scoping.
- Pen test: Redwood accepts customer-initiated pen tests with the following guardrails: 14 business days notice for red-team / full-scope tests; 5 business days for lower-impact scans. All testing is expected to be performed against non-production (staging) unless explicit, documented agreement otherwise.
- Audit rights & evidence cadence: propose weekly evidence bundles during the initial onboarding window (first 8 weeks) containing the manifest items (logs, configuration snapshots, SOC artifact pointers). After onboarding, a quarterly evidence snapshot is provided for the agreed artifacts. Emergency ad-hoc requests will be triaged via the security contact and limited to scoped data per order form.

Other proposed controls included in the draft: limited inspection hours (business hours M–F), max on-site/interactive inspection duration of 3 business days per rolling 12 months, and requirement for a signed non-disclosure for any external testers.

I'll leave this with Ben (legal) and Laura (compliance) for internal sign-off; happy to join a call tomorrow at 10:00 PT if that works for you.

Olga
Director, Assurance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sec_exhibit_draft_v1.pdf (attachment stub), evidence_manifest_template.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Security exhibit / audit rights clarification for order form — legal redline notes

Thanks for the draft, Olga. High level this is directionally good — a few legal redline asks to reduce operational risk while keeping the customer happy:

1) Inspection scope: change any absolute "staging-only" phrasing to "staging by default; production access may be allowed only with explicit written approval and under Redwood supervision" — protects against ambiguous emergency scenarios.
2) Notice window: we can accept 14 business days for standard pen tests, but propose 21 business days for tests that would exercise IDS/IPS or large-scale scans (we can gate by test classification in the exhibit).
3) Limit inspection frequency/duration: suggest a cap of 4 business days total per rolling 12-month period for interactive inspections (on-site or live sessions).
4) Access controls: forbid direct customer VPN into production; require jumpbox with IP allowlist and session recording for any live interactive testing.
5) Evidence privacy: evidence manifests that include customer-identifiable logs must be redacted and provided via secure share; Redwood retains right to redact any platform-level sensitive data not attributable to the customer.
6) Indemnity carveouts: legal requests a short clause clarifying that Redwood is not liable for customer test activities outside the agreed scope or for customer-supplied tooling that modifies platform behavior.

Action items: Olga — can you produce a short compromise paragraph for the exhibit that incorporates 2 & 3 above? Laura — can you review the indemnity language and confirm we can accept 21 days for high-risk tests if we get the additional gating? Karthik — is the jumpbox/session-recording requirement operationally feasible?

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Counsel
Redwood Inference
